properties.summary: European Council President António Costa is warning governments that they will be worse off if they fail to agree to new EU-wide taxes to finance the bloc’s next seven-year budget. properties.title: Slovenian parliament lifts former PM Golob’s immunity in police-meddling probe
properties.summary: Slovenia’s parliament on Wednesday allowed prosecutors to pursue a criminal case against former Prime Minister Robert Golob over allegations that he improperly meddled in police staffing after taking office in 2022. All 75 lawmakers present — including Golob himself — voted against granting him parliamentary immunity, allowing proceedings to move forward. properties.title: Andy Burnham will attend COP31
properties.summary: LONDON — New U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham will attend the U.N. climate conference COP31 in Turkey this November. In his first address to the House of Commons as prime minister, Burnham directly linked the devastating floods in Nepal and China to “the climate crisis” and confirmed that he would go the summit. properties.summary: LONDON — U.K. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is to attend a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Ireland as he pushes for closer ties with Europe. properties.summary: Frank Furedi announces resignation from MCC Brussels after organisation’s staff ‘not paid in July or August’ The head of Viktor Orbán’s favourite Brussels thinktank has quit, citing unpaid wages since the change of government in Hungary. The sociology professor Frank Furedi said he was resigning as the executive director of MCC Brussels with “immediate effect” on Monday over “persistent failure to provide the contractually agreed funds”.
